sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: head in dorsal view almost black on the anterior 1/3, grading to rusty orange over the posterior 2/3; frontal margin stout, widest at the middle, with a median notch, the middle of its posterior margin forming a square pointed projection, unlike most species of the genus, which have a rounded, blunt posterior margin; antennae 11—13-segmented, mostly 12. Alate: antennae 13—16-segmented, mostly 15 or 16, segment formula 2>3<4=5; pronotum subsquare, distinctly narrower than the head width (including the compound eyes). Closest to C. undulans, in which the head capsule sculpture is deeper and finer and the frontal margin narrower and more wrinkled.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body dull pale yellow-brown. Head yellow-brown, with a pale brown transverse band between the compound eyes; the chevron mark on the wing scale indistinct. In the forewing the radial vein, the radial sector (including its first branch) and the anterior margin of the basal half of the wing are pale brown, the distal branches of the radial sector and the anterior margin very pale brown to nearly white, the wing membrane transparent. Pronotum yellow-brown, the white midline and transverse band present or absent. Abdominal tergites pale yellow-brown to pale brown; antennae pale brown; labrum pale yellow-brown; femora yellowish white, the ends of the legs pale yellow-brown; sternites pale yellow. Head subsquare, the cranial sutures almost undeveloped. Compound eyes medium-sized, nearly oval. Ocelli medium-sized, oval, almost touching the compound eyes. Antennae 13—16-segmented, mostly 15 or 16, the segment formula variable, often 2>3<4=5. Pronotum subsquare, its width clearly less than the head width (including the compound eyes); anterior margin shallowly concave, the sides moderately convex, the posterior margin almost straight. Radial vein of the forewing joining the anterior margin at 1/3 of the distance from the wing base; radial sector with 6 branches. Arolia present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head almost black on the anterior 1/3 in dorsal view, grading to rusty orange over the posterior 2/3; in lateral view nearly black on the anterior 1/2, grading posteriorly to rusty orange. Mandibles dark chestnut brown. Anterior margin of the pronotum with a rusty internal process and rim, the remainder contrasting white. Head capsule in dorsal view with distinct notches on the anterior and posterior margins of the frontal margin; head short, the sides almost parallel, usually slightly constricted behind the frontal margin and convex behind the middle; posterior corners rounded, the posterior margin straight or almost so; middle of the vertex with a small, shallow depression. Frontal margin stout, widest at the middle, with a median notch, clearly delimited posteriorly from the vertex, the middle of its posterior part forming a square pointed projection. Sculpture overall shallow but dense (including the frontal margin), weaker in the concavity of the frontal face. Frontal face about 1.5 times as wide as high; in lateral view the frontal face meets the vertex face at 90°. Labrum short, its base subsquare, the apex slightly swollen and blunt, sometimes with slight lateral depressions. Frontal horns variable in size, mostly blunt, continuous with the frontal margin; their inner face deeply concave and widely separated from the clypeus; directed forward. Genal horns weakly warty, ill-defined from the genae. Frontal horns and genal horns far apart. Mandibles of medium length, slightly swollen and distinctly angled at the base, the apex short and falcate, almost horizontal in lateral view; the first marginal tooth of both mandibles distinct. Compound eyes small or very small, but usually discernible. Antennae 11—13-segmented, mostly 12, the segment formula variable. Pronotum broad, shield-shaped; the sides almost parallel or slightly convex; anterior margin shallowly concave; laterally biconvex and weakly undulate. Posterior margin almost straight. Closest to C. undulans, in which the head capsule sculpture is deeper and finer and the frontal margin narrower and more wrinkled.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: This is the commonest native drywood termite of the Dominican Republic (75 of 118 native Cryptotermes samples), widely distributed along the northern and eastern coasts; it is allopatric with C. rotundiceps. Type locality: 0.5 km west of Club Mediterraneo, La Altagracia Province, Dominican Republic.
